acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-01 — A bash wrapper bin/event-push exists that resolves the built @personal-events/s3-repository CLI and execs it, forwarding all arguments and stdin verbatim, including arguments containing spaces, quotes and glob characters.

verification.definingInputProperty: Arguments that actually contain a space, a quote and a glob character — not simple tokens
verification.assertions: Each argument arrives at the CLI byte-identical; stdin is forwarded unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-02 — The wrapper contains no event logic — no key construction, no JSON assembly, no validation, no priority/type checking. Resolution and delegation only. This is the guardrail that keeps the object-key contract to a single implementation.

verification.assertions: No event-type literal, no key/JSON assembly, no priority range check appears in the script

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-03 — Resolution follows the documented order EVENT_PUSH_HOME > symlink-resolved location of the wrapper itself. When the wrapper is reached through one or more symlinks, it resolves its own real path back to the repository checkout and locates packages/s3-repository/dist/main.js from there.

verification.definingInputProperty: Invocation through a symlink located in a different directory from the repo, including a chained link → link → script case
verification.assertions: Both single and double symlink invocations resolve and run --dry-run successfully; EVENT_PUSH_HOME takes precedence when both are available

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-04 — The wrapper has a #!/usr/bin/env bash shebang, runs correctly when invoked from both bash and zsh, uses only command invocations that behave identically on macOS and Linux (no GNU-only readlink -f, no realpath dependency), and passes shellcheck with zero warnings at default severity.

verification.definingInputProperty: The wrapper source, checked for GNU-only constructs that shellcheck on Linux will not flag
verification.assertions: shellcheck reports zero warnings; neither readlink -f nor realpath appears

verification.command: zsh -c 'bash bin/event-push --type alert --priority 1 --source t --name t --bucket x --dry-run'
verification.definingInputProperty: Invocation from a zsh parent shell rather than bash
verification.assertions: Exit 0 under zsh as well as bash

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-05 — Running event-push from an arbitrary working directory (verified from at least /tmp and $HOME) works.

verification.definingInputProperty: Working directories outside the repo checkout — /tmp and $HOME specifically
verification.assertions: Exit 0 and a printed key from each directory

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-06 — Cron's minimal environment is an explicit, executed test case: the wrapper resolves correctly with no shell profile sourced, no nvm on $PATH, and a bare environment (env -i). The failure mode where the tool works interactively but silently fails under cron must be demonstrated absent, not merely assumed.

verification.definingInputProperty: A genuinely empty environment via env -i with only a minimal PATH — no profile, no nvm, no inherited variables
verification.assertions: Exit 0 and a printed key both WITH EVENT_PUSH_HOME set and WITHOUT it (proving self-resolution works bare, not merely the override)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-07 — A documented $PATH installation path exists — a symlink from ~/.local/bin/event-push to bin/event-push — and the wrapper still resolves correctly when invoked through that symlink (this is the case AC-03's symlink resolution exists for).

verification.definingInputProperty: Invocation via a symlink in a $PATH directory outside the repo
verification.assertions: The symlinked invocation resolves and succeeds; README documents the exact ln -s command

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-08 — A non-zero exit from the underlying CLI propagates unchanged through the wrapper: exit codes 2, 3 and 4 from @personal-events/s3-repository are observed unmodified by the caller.

verification.definingInputProperty: Invocations that make the underlying CLI exit 2, 3 and 4 — not ones that make the wrapper itself fail
verification.assertions: The observed exit code equals exactly 2, 3, 4 respectively — not merely non-zero, since collapsing all failures to 1 would destroy the branchable contract

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-09 — A recipes document ships containing at least these four working, copy-pasteable recipes: a crontab entry, a git post-merge (or post-commit) hook, a CI step, and a "notify me when this long-running job finishes" one-liner that pushes a different priority on success versus failure.

verification.definingInputProperty: The complete enumerated recipe set — crontab, git hook, CI step, success/failure one-liner
verification.assertions: All four named recipes are present as headings; the success/failure one-liner additionally executes in dry-run form proving it is valid shell rather than prose

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-10 — The one remaining hand-built object key in the plan tree is retrofitted. .agents/plans/local-sync-client/s3-poll-core.md (AWE-152 — S3 poll core) line ~236 currently validates by running aws s3 cp exemplars/valid-github.json s3://<bucket>/<built-key>; it is updated in this same change to use event-push. A repo-wide guard asserts no plan file, script, or doc instructs a human to construct an object key by hand.

verification.command: ! rg -n 'aws s3 cp .*s3://' .agents/plans/ docs/ bin/ packages/ && rg -q 'event-push' .agents/plans/local-sync-client/s3-poll-core.md
verification.definingInputProperty: The complete plan/docs/bin/packages tree, not only this feature's directory
verification.assertions: Zero hand-built-key instructions remain anywhere; the specific retrofit target now references event-push

acceptanceCriteria.explicitUserApproval: AC-10 supersedes the stub's original criterion naming AWE-151 and AWE-152 as retrofit targets. AWE-151 was re-planned 2026-08-31 and no longer uses aws s3 cp; AWE-152 now belongs to the local-sync-client feature. Recorded 2026-08-31.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-11 — Failure modes produce clear messages and non-zero exits: the built CLI cannot be located (message names exactly what to build or which variable to set, and exits non-zero), and node is unavailable on $PATH (message names the missing runtime).

verification.definingInputProperty: An unbuilt CLI path, and a PATH from which node is genuinely absent
verification.assertions: Non-zero exit in both cases; the unbuilt-CLI message names both 'pnpm build' and EVENT_PUSH_HOME; the missing-runtime message names node

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-12 — Guidance conformance per .agents/languages/shell.md, verified by shellcheck.

verification.definingInputProperty: Both shell artifacts produced by this story
verification.assertions: shellcheck reports zero warnings for both files

entryPoints.entryPoint: bin/event-push invoked under a bare cron-like environment
